newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CUP FINAL REF CALLS FOR ELECTRONIC AIDS IN LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CUP FINAL REF CALLS FOR ELECTRONIC AIDS IN LEAGUE.

text.p: English League Cup final referee Martin Bodenham on Tuesday called for electronic goal-judging aids and time keepers to be used in premier league matches.

Bodenham, who will be in charge of the Cup final replay between Leicester and Middlesbrough on Wednesday, forecast the changes following a series of blunders by officials which have been highlighted by television cameras.

Referee David Elleray became the latest official to come under the microscope when a shot by Chesterfield's Jonathan Howard in Sunday's F.A. Cup semifinal with Middlesbrough crashed down from the crossbar over the goal line, then bounced away, but the goal was not given.
Bodenham said: "Very soon there will be some sort of electronic system that tells you whether the ball has crossed the line or not.
"It's physically impossible on some occasions for a linesman to be in the correct position."
Although Bodenham ruled out using cameras to decide on awarding penalties, he does consider there is room for an official timekeeper.
He said: "At the end of 90 minutes a guy sticks a board up which tells you there are five minutes left for injury time, substitutions or whatever.
"It will take the responsibility away from referees. It will also take away the possibility of confrontation between a manager and a referee because he will know exactly how long there is."
